boundary_evidence: WHOLE RUN, 71 of 71. tools/tu_map.py calls 0x0210428c..0x02107858 one contiguous linker run of 71 function(s) (build/tu_map.json), and this TU licenses all of it, ROM ordinals 0..70. There is no sourceless hole: every one of the 71 addresses has a legacy src/ file AND an entry in config/arm9/overlays/ov006/delinks.txt, and `tools/tubuild.py inspect ov006/dScMgPanel_c` reports `functions without complete : none` and `functions with no legacy source : none`. That is the difference from the sibling dScMgTeresa_c, which could license only 48 of 81.

LEFT EDGE (high). 0x0210428c is _ZN12dScMgPanel_cD1Ev, the class's key function and the lowest address of the run. Vtable slot 16 relocates to it. The function below it, 0x02104278, belongs to the preceding unattributed span.

RIGHT EDGE (medium). The run ends at 0x02107858, where dScMgPanel_c_classInit begins (size 0x34, src/d_s_mg_panel.c). tu_map splits that factory out as its own 1-function unattributed span 0x02107858..0x0210788c, and every promoted ov006 sibling follows the same convention -- dScMgRoulette_c's landed manifest licenses 0x0210788c..0x0210a400 while its own classInit at 0x0210a400 stays a separate shard. The factory is NOT folded in here. tu_map's own right-edge confidence for this run is medium and ov006 is a module it reports as under-segmented, so 71 is a lower bound on what one original file held rather than a proven file boundary.

THE VTABLE CORROBORATES BOTH ENDS. Of the 36 slots, six relocate into this run -- slot 0 to 0x021073b0, slot 6 to 0x02107358, slot 9 to 0x0210730c, slot 16 to 0x0210428c, slot 17 to 0x021042b0, slot 18 to 0x021071fc -- and every one of the other 30 relocates OUTSIDE 0x0210428c..0x02107858, into ov004 or arm9. Both ends of the claimed range are this class's own code.

NOT CLAIMED, and deliberately so: __sinit_ov006_02131fa4 (0x02131fa4, size 0x318, src/__sinit_ov006_02131fa4.c) is this class's static initializer and lives in ov006's .init section with its own delinks.txt block and .ctor slot. The original translation unit was therefore NOT text-only -- it owned .data, .bss and .init output as well -- but ov006's entire .data segment is one section owned by no file, so only .text is claimable. The 27 eight-byte {function pointer, 0} objects at 0x0213dc4c..0x0213dd34 that hold this class's callback addresses stay extern; they are 27 SEPARATE objects rather than one descriptor table (g_profile_MG_PANEL sits inside the cluster at 0x0213dc64 with a different shape and a different owner, and the sinit loads each address individually in scrambled order), and what clusters them is mwld laying .data out by ascending object size.
notes: Hand-assembled from the 71 legacy shards; tools/tubuild.py create ran, and its generated preamble was DISCARDED WHOLE rather than repaired. At 71 members it carried the failure modes writer.md documents: two contradictory PMF typedefs, three incompatible `struct C` bodies (0x4692 pad / 0x4674 pad / derived from a 36-virtual base), two incompatible `Obj` typedefs, and data_0209d454 declared both as a scalar and as an array. The shipped file follows ov002/Player: every member keeps its own declarations inside its own body and nothing is canonicalised.

decl_common.h is deliberately NOT included, and this is a departure from the daDsnBase_c / daObjCtMecha03_c / dScMgTeresa_c precedent. It declares ten of this TU's own members and seven of the ten contradict the shard that defines them: func_ov006_02104354 and func_ov006_02104ac4 on the RETURN TYPE (`int` against the shards' `void`), and func_ov006_021042e8, 02104b5c, 02104d44, 02104d94 and 02105ab4 on the parameter type (`void*` against `char*` or a shadow struct). Including it makes each of those an `illegal function overloading` error against a body that already matches byte-for-byte. ov002/Player, the largest promoted TU in the tree, excludes it for the same reason. The four class-method members that used to lean on it -- ordinals 67-70 -- now carry the declarations they actually used, copied verbatim from decl_common.h to BLOCK scope inside their own bodies, so those spellings are unchanged; the other 67 members never see them.

One member needed a source change the merge forced. include/dScMgBase_c.h:12 declares `extern "C" void *data_ov004_020beb68;` at file scope, and ordinal 60 (func_ov006_02106ca4) recovered the same ROM object as `char *`. The block-scope licence covers FUNCTIONS with C linkage, not a second declaration of one variable with a different type, so the shard's view is spelled as a reinterpreting read of the header's object -- `#define PANEL_BEB68 (*(char **)&data_ov004_020beb68)` -- rather than a redeclaration. Same address, same load width, no extra local, and the member matches.

Ordinals 0 and 1 are two shards of ONE C++ definition. src/_ZN12dScMgPanel_cD1Ev.cpp and src/_ZN12dScMgPanel_cD0Ev.cpp each spell `dScMgPanel_c::~dScMgPanel_c() {}`; merged, writing both would be a duplicate definition. The file carries the body once, under ordinal 0, and mwcc emits D1, D0 and a homeless D2 from it.

Eight bracketed optimisation pragmas across three families, not the seven notes/data/tu-promotion-queue.tsv claims: opt_common_subs off on ordinals 3, 4, 6, 50 and 57; opt_strength_reduction off on 51 and 53; opt_propagation off on 60. `tools/tubuild.py inspect` prints 8 and a direct grep of the 71 shards finds the same eight files. Each keeps its own #pragma push / #pragma pop bracket, which binds positionally only because `#pragma defer_codegen off` is at the top of the file; with codegen deferred the state that binds is the state at end of file and the bracket is worth zero members. That pragma also emits .text in SOURCE order rather than reversed, which is why this file is written ROM-ascending -- one decision, not two.

CONTROLS, measured at this revision on the shipped file, both required by notes/agents/roles/writer.md before claiming a pragma does anything. (A) Delete all eight pragma brackets outright, change nothing else: 67/71, and the four DIFFs are func_ov006_0210446c, 02106664, 021067a4 and 02106aa8. So four of the eight are load-bearing and the other four -- 02104354, 02104580, 021063a0, 02106ca4 -- are inert at plain -O4,p in this TU; they are kept because they are what the shards recovered and deleting them buys nothing. (B) Delete ONLY `#pragma defer_codegen off`, keep every bracket: 67/71 -- byte-identical to deleting the pragmas outright, because the bracket binds to nothing while codegen is deferred -- AND emission order inverts to "70 ordinal pair(s) NOT in ROM order", which linkcheck [4b/8] refuses. One pragma buys the bytes and the order together, exactly as writer.md predicts.
The queue row's shard_count of 72 counts src/d_s_mg_panel.c (dScMgPanel_c_classInit); this promotion absorbs 71 shards, not 72.
